The titanium tubes in this type of heat exchanger are used because they are resistant to corrosion and have a high thermal conductivity, which makes them ideal for transferring heat.

The main components of a heat exchanger, including the titanium tubes, include the shell, the tube sheet, the baffles, and the coolant. The shell is the outer casing of the heat exchanger, and the tube sheet is the plate that supports the tubes and separates the hot and cold fluids. The baffles are the plates that direct the fluid flow through the heat exchanger, and the coolant is the fluid that flows through the heat exchanger to transfer heat.

The titanium tubes are typically brazed or welded to the tube sheet, and are then sealed with a gasket. The fluid that flows through the tubes is typically water, and the fluid that flows through the shell is typically steam. The heat exchanger also includes a pressure control system that maintains the pressure drop across the heat exchanger at a constant level, regardless of the flow rate.

The pressure control system includes a pressure control valve that is located in the flow path of the coolant. The pressure control valve is adjusted to maintain the desired pressure drop across the heat exchanger. The heat exchanger also includes a temperature control system that maintains the temperature of the steam at a constant level. The temperature control system includes a temperature sensor that is located in the steam flow path, and a control valve that adjusts the flow rate of the coolant based on the temperature sensor signal.
